title: ws_frame_logging plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ws_frame_logging` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component WsFrameLoggingConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

WsFrameLoggingConfig.description:
Configuration for the `ws_frame_logging` plugin. Logs WebSocket message
metadata (direction, frame type, payload size, optional payload
fingerprint, Close code / reason length) under the `ws_frame_log`
tracing target after the shared H1/H2/H3 relay successfully delivers
the final post-plugin message (`outcome=delivered`), and records every
gateway-published policy Close separately (`outcome=policy_close`).
Granularity is one record per complete (reassembled) message, not per
wire frame: a Text/Binary message sent as several fragments produces
one record whose `size_bytes` is the reassembled payload length
(inflated length under `websocket_permessage_deflate: terminate`), and
the disconnect record's `frames_*` counters count delivered messages.
Logs Text and Binary messages by default; Ping/Pong are opt-in via
`log_ping_pong`. Peer Close frames are logged on the delivery path with
`close_code` / `close_reason_len` (raw reason text is never logged).
`size_bytes` for Close with a status code is `2 + reason.len()`. The
plugin never transforms or drops frames — it is purely observational.
Cancelled or failed destination writes produce no frame event; frame
and disconnect `frames_*` / `bytes_*` counters share that success-only
boundary. Disconnect records also emit `io_side` (`read`/`write`/`none`),
success-only `bytes_c2b` / `bytes_b2c`, and `termination_reason` (the
relay's bounded session-end classification, e.g. `normal_peer_close`,
`relay_error`, `idle_timeout`, `drain`, `max_lifetime`). On HTTP/3, a
client-side QUIC write/FIN failure after the relay accepted the final
Close is attributed on the disconnect record (`backend_to_client` /
`write`).

`policy_close` records are emitted once per relay-half decision after
the full decision is known, independent of this plugin's priority
(including under `priority_override`): a terminal Close from any
`on_ws_frame` plugin, a fragment-budget Close, and parser rejections of
an inbound message (plugin or global frame/message size ceilings,
incomplete-message bounds, terminated `permessage-deflate` faults).
Session-level stops and relay transport faults are reported on the
disconnect record instead. Every frame, policy-close, and disconnect
record carries `plugin_id` (the plugin-config resource id, `-` when
unattributed) so multiple effective instances stay distinguishable.

Volume controls (`sample_rate`, `direction`,
`max_records_per_connection`) select `delivered` records only;
`policy_close` and disconnect records are always emitted at the
configured level.

Default `log_level` is `info` so healthy frame traffic does not become
warning-level noise. Under the gateway's default
`FERRUM_LOG_LEVEL=warn` EnvFilter, constructing an enabled empty config
emits an actionable construction-time warning naming the filtered level
while normal frame records remain suppressed. Validation and cache
publication can construct an instance separately, so the diagnostic can
repeat. A filter stricter than `warn` (or `ws_frame_log=off`) also
suppresses that diagnostic; operators using such a filter must
deliberately admit the configured target level. Explicit `trace` or
`debug` likewise require a matching (or more verbose) runtime filter;
`warn` is available only when selected deliberately. Filtering skips
fingerprint computation and tracing event construction only — frame
parsing, plugin selection (`requires_ws_frame_hooks`), `on_ws_frame` /
`on_ws_policy_close` dispatch, delivery prepare/emit, and disconnect
dispatch still occur, so H1 raw-copy tunnel mode remains unavailable
while this plugin is attached.

Admission contract: only the keys below are allowed; unknown keys and
explicit `null` field values are rejected. `payload_preview_bytes`
values above 65536 are rejected (not clamped). The plugin is registered
KeepLastKnownGood, like every log sink. Admin create/update performs
strict construction and returns HTTP 400 for an invalid enabled config
before storing it. File-mode load and `ferrum-edge validate` fail, and
a DB/CP/DP reload whose invalid enabled config cannot be constructed is
rejected so the previously published plugin generation keeps
serving.

Raw frame contents are never logged: WebSocket payloads routinely carry
credentials (bearer tokens, cookies, API keys), so when
`include_payload_preview` is enabled the `preview` field contains only a
keyed, non-reversible fingerprint of the form
`hmac-sha256:<12 hex chars> len=<bytes>` (with a trailing `+` after the
digest when only a prefix of the payload was hashed). The key is
generated per plugin instance and is not exposed in logs, so log access
alone cannot confirm guessed payloads offline. Close reasons are treated
as application payload and are never logged in the clear.

log_level.description: Tracing level for frame log output. Case-sensitive; unknown values (e.g., `"error"`, `"INFO"`) and explicit `null` are rejected at config load time. Healthy records default to `info`; construction warns when the active filter suppresses the configured level.

include_payload_preview.description: Emit a keyed, non-reversible payload fingerprint (`hmac-sha256:<prefix> len=<n>`) in the `preview` field. Raw frame bytes are never logged. Explicit `null` is rejected.

payload_preview_bytes.description: Maximum number of leading payload bytes folded into the fingerprint digest. Values above 65536 are rejected (not clamped). Must be greater than zero when `include_payload_preview` is true; zero is accepted only when previews are disabled. Explicit `null` is rejected.

log_ping_pong.description: Whether to log ping/pong frames in addition to text/binary frames. Explicit `null` is rejected.

sample_rate.description: Fraction of WebSocket connections whose `delivered` records are emitted. Sampling is deterministic per connection (a session is either fully recorded or not), so a sampled session stays coherent; unsampled sessions skip fingerprinting entirely. `0` emits no `delivered` records while keeping `policy_close` and disconnect records. Values outside 0–1, non-numbers, and explicit `null` are rejected.

direction.description: Relay direction whose `delivered` records are emitted. Does not filter `policy_close` or disconnect records. Case-sensitive; unknown values and explicit `null` are rejected.

max_records_per_connection.description: Maximum `delivered` records emitted per WebSocket connection, shared by both directions. `0` (default) is unlimited. When a connection reaches the cap the plugin emits one `event=record_cap_reached` record and suppresses further `delivered` records for that connection; `policy_close` and disconnect records are not capped. Explicit `null` is rejected.
